question: Partly shared. Both papers address progression from MCI to AD (progressive against stable MCI) among ADNI MCI participants, so the task, comparison and population class match. The recorded comparison, however, sets P-334's univariate florbetaben amyloid-PET AUC (0.84) against P-211's Explainable Boosting Machine on baseline structural MRI, cognitive scores, demographics and APOE4 (0.92). P-211 uses no PET, so the channel being compared is not shared, and condition 1 fails for the pair as recorded. P-334 also prints single-feature AUCs on channels P-211 does use (ADAS13 0.83, mPACCtrailsB 0.83, hippocampal volume 0.75), so a shared-channel comparison exists and is judged under conditions 3 and 4. Allowed differences: P-334 fits no model and labels visit records (pMCI records only within the 3 years before conversion); P-211 predicts from baseline at fixed 1- to 5-year horizons with a 90/10 split and 5-fold CV.
metric: ROC-AUC with ROC-AUC (match). P-334's values are univariate, record-level descriptive AUCs with no fitted model and no validation; P-211's are cross-validated or test-set AUCs of a multivariable model.

figures.P-334: Univariate AUCs, no interval printed (Table 2): FBB 0.84, ADAS13 0.83, mPACCtrailsB 0.83, hippocampus 0.75. Derived Hanley-McNeil intervals at the participant counts (348 pMCI, 487 sMCI). The paper does not print how many participants have an FBB value, so for FBB this is the narrowest possible interval. FBB 0.84: Q1 = A/(2-A) = 0.7241, Q2 = 2A^2/(1+A) = 0.7670, SE^2 = [0.84*0.16 + 347*(0.7241-0.7056) + 486*(0.7670-0.7056)]/(348*487) = 36.39/169476, SE = 0.0147, 95% CI [0.811, 0.869]. ADAS13 0.83: SE = 0.0150, CI [0.801, 0.859]. Hippocampus 0.75: SE = 0.0176, CI [0.716, 0.784]. The unit is the visit record, not the participant, so these intervals also ignore within-person clustering and are too narrow if anything.
figures.P-211: Comb. (a) (MRI + cognitive scores + age, gender, education, baseline diagnosis, APOE4); no interval printed (Figure 2 shows SD error bars only). 5-year model: mean CV AUC about 0.92 (abstract: accuracy 85%, AUC 0.92). Derived Hanley-McNeil at the 5-year sample (Table 1: 85 dementia, 140 MCI): Q1 = 0.8519, Q2 = 0.8817, SE^2 = [0.92*0.08 + 84*(0.8519-0.8464) + 139*(0.8817-0.8464)]/(85*140) = 5.434/11900, SE = 0.0214, CI [0.878, 0.962] (at the 90% training share, 77/126: [0.876, 0.964]). 3-year model on the test set (10% of 580 = 188 dementia + 392 MCI, so about 19 converters and 39 stable): AUC 0.81 with interaction effects, Q1 = 0.6807, Q2 = 0.7250, SE = 0.0659, CI [0.681, 0.939]; 0.78 without interaction effects, SE = 0.0696, CI [0.644, 0.916].

matched_figure_check: A matched figure exists for the horizon. P-334 labels pMCI records only within the 3 years before conversion, which corresponds to P-211's 3-year model. P-211's printed 3-year test AUC (0.81, CI [0.681, 0.939]) contains P-334's FBB 0.84, ADAS13 and mPACCtrailsB 0.83 and the ADAS family (0.80-0.83). P-334's ADAS13 interval [0.801, 0.859] contains 0.81. The FBB interval at the largest possible n [0.811, 0.869] misses 0.81 by 0.001, and at any smaller FBB n it contains it. P-211's 3-year mean CV AUC is shown only in Figure 2 as the 'low point' and is not printed as a number. At the matched horizon the papers agree within uncertainty, so the headline gap (0.84 against 0.92) is a 3-year against 5-year difference that the papers' own figures dissolve.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply: no compared AUC reaches 0.97 (maximum 0.92). P-211 has 1042 participants, a 10% test split and 5-fold CV. P-334 fits no model, so near-ceiling overfitting is not at issue.
reason: As recorded, the pair compares an amyloid-PET univariate AUC (P-334) with an MRI-plus-cognition model that contains no PET (P-211), so the channel is not shared (condition 1). On the shared cognitive and MRI channels and at the matched 3-year horizon, P-211's test AUC of 0.81 (derived CI 0.681-0.939) and P-334's AUCs of 0.83-0.84 fall within each other's intervals (condition 3). The headline 0.84 against 0.92 is beyond uncertainty only because it sets P-334's 3-year labelling window against P-211's 5-year model.

quotes.quote: Our findings showed the strong predictive potential of PET, particularly florbetaben (FBB), which achieved an AUC of 0.84.
In labeling the data for pMCI and sMCI, we shift our focus from participants to individual records
Only records preceding the AD diagnosis and those within the 3-year window before the conversion event receive labels.
With AUC values of 0.80, 0.83, and 0.82, respectively, these tests effectively differentiate between sMCI and pMCI participants
The five-years prediction accuracy reached 85% (AUC = 0.92) using both cognitive scores and MRI markers.
The dataset is divided into training and test sets with a percentage, respectively, of 90% and 10%.
Comb. (a) both MRI-driven biomarkers and cognitive test scores, plus age, gender, education, diagnose at baseline, and APOE4.

The mean AUC using Comb (a) displayed a characteristic pattern of first at about 0.9, then decreasing, reaching a low point at 3 years, followed by a gradual increase until 5 years of follow-up, to about 0.92.

The main performance indicators, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC, were 0.75, 0.78, 0.73, and 0.81 (with interaction effects) compared to 0.72, 0.76, 0.68, and 0.78 (without interaction effects), respectively.
